The test image shows a close-up of a soybean petiole/stem with dark brown to reddish-brown irregular blotches extending along the length. Green pods are visible in the background. No white mold, no leaf lesions visible — this is a stem/petiole symptom.

Top candidates: **Anthracnose** (red-dark brown blotches on petioles), **Diaporthe** (stem blight with pycnidia), **Phytophthora** (dark brown stem lesion).

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Close-up of a hairy soybean petiole with dark reddish-brown to dark brown irregular blotches spreading along the length, with green pods visible in background.
- **Anthracnose** reference (bottom-left panel): Shows a petiole with nearly identical dark brown irregular blotches — exact match in color, texture, and pattern.
- **Diaporthe**: Shows stem canker with pycnidia (black specks in rows) and wilting — different pattern.
- **Phytophthora**: Dark brown lesion restricted to base of stem, root rot — not matching.
- **Rhizoctonia/Brown Stem Rot/Septoria**: Leaf lesions, seedling damping-off, or internal stem browning — none match.

The dark, irregular reddish-brown blotches on a petiole near green pods is the hallmark of Anthracnose stem blight.
